records.name: Philadelphia Boys and Girls Gymnastics
records.summary: A gymnastics club for kids. It coaches boys from age 5 to 18 on the competitive path, and it also runs preschool and beginner classes for girls.
records.what_you_do: Kids take gymnastics classes in the fall, winter and spring sessions. New families can book a free trial lesson before they enroll.

schedule.text: Fall, winter and spring class sessions. Set class times are not listed on the website.

cost.text: Not listed on the website. A free trial lesson is offered.

first_step.how: Call 215-204-7452 or email info@philadelphiaboysgymnastics.org to book a free trial lesson, or register for the current session online.
first_step.basis: Beginner and preschool classes exist and a free trial lesson is offered, so the way to start is clear.

records.notes: IRS legal name is Philadelphia Boys Gymnastics. The IRS street address (535 N 22nd St) differs from the address on the site, so the site address is used. The site header says Boys & Girls and the footer says Boys'. Newest dated item is an Aug 3, 2026 news post about fall, winter and spring enrollment; its exact URL was not captured, so the homepage is cited. Gymnastics has no exact tag; sports-teams and youth_coaching are the closest.

records.name: Philadelphia Wind Symphony
records.summary: A wind band of about 50 players that gives around six concerts a season. Players join by audition, or sign up as substitutes.
records.what_you_do: Musicians play in the season concerts, from fall into early summer. Substitutes can join on any wind, brass or percussion part at any time.

schedule.text: About six concerts a season. The 2026 to 2027 season lists October, December, March, May and June concerts. The next one is Trick or Treat on October 31 at 11 am.

cost.text: The Trick or Treat concert is free. Membership or audition costs are not stated.

first_step.how: Email info@philadelphiawindsymphony.org or check the auditions page for substitute openings. You can also hear the group at the free Trick or Treat concert on October 31 at 11 am.
first_step.basis: Seats are filled by audition and the 2026 to 2027 auditions are closed. Substitute spots stay open, so the way in is clear but needs a musical audition.

records.notes: Legal name in the IRS filing is Philadelphia Chamber Winds. The site uses the same PO Box and the founder named on the filing, so it is treated as the same group. The site calls the group both a professional ensemble and a 51-member volunteer ensemble; the summary follows the volunteer wording. The concert venue address is not on the page. The page does not give a year for the October concert; the 2026 to 2027 season listing is the basis for status. Rehearsal times are not published.

records.name: Philadelphia Community Cats Council
records.notes: Tier 1 check could not confirm what this group does. The website on the IRS filing (www.phillycats.org) returned an empty page on two fetches. Needs a retry of the site or a human check. No summary, categories or interests were written, so this record should be held back.

records.name: Philadelphia Crosstown Coalition
records.summary: A nonpartisan coalition of community groups, mostly registered neighborhood organizations, that works on zoning, affordable housing and property tax issues.
records.what_you_do: Member groups send delegates to the meetings, join the zoning and land use, affordable housing or tax committees, and help elect the board each year.

schedule.text: Meetings are listed for the fourth Monday of most months, September through June, at 6:30 pm, at changing locations. The site also says meetings are held about six times a year.

locations.label: Meeting place (changes; a recent one was String Theory School)

cost.text: Member dues are charged; the amount is not published.

first_step.how: Groups thinking about joining can attend a meeting as guests. Questions can go to the contact on the website.
first_step.basis: Guests can attend, but voting membership is for dues-paying community groups, and the way in for individuals is not described.

records.notes: The site header says Philadelphia Crosstown Coalition of Civics; the body text says Philadelphia Crosstown Coalition. The site says it was founded in 2008. The only date on the site is a 2015 copyright line, which is not evidence, and no dated news is posted. A meeting notice on the page features a flyer for 3rd Congressional District candidates. The group calls itself nonpartisan, but a reviewer should check that before publishing. The site's contact is one person's personal email, which was not copied here. Status is probably_active only because the site loads and lists meeting details.

records.name: Philadelphia Heritage Chorale
records.summary: A mixed-age choir that sings many kinds of music, with a focus on music from the African diaspora.
records.what_you_do: Singers perform with the chorale in its concerts. The site does not explain how to audition or how rehearsals work.

cost.text: Not published for singers. The site has donation and support pages.

first_step.how: Email PHLHeritageChorale@gmail.com to ask about rehearsals and how to audition.
first_step.basis: The way in is unclear: the site publishes no rehearsal, audition or membership details.

records.notes: Legal name is Philadelphia Heritage Chorale Inc. The mailing address is a P.O. Box only, so no meeting location was recorded. The only date on the site is a 2021 copyright line, which is not evidence. The site loads and lists no dated items, so probably_active rests on a working site with no dates. The events link goes to a services page. The email is the one published on the site.

records.name: Philadelphia Liberty Tennis Association
records.summary: A tennis group open to LGBTQ+ players and allies across the Philadelphia area and the wider Delaware Valley. It runs drills and events and is a USTA community tennis association.
records.what_you_do: Members play tennis with the group and join its drills and events, such as the October drills at Riverwinds Golf and Tennis Club.

schedule.text: No regular schedule is published. Drills at Riverwinds Golf and Tennis Club at 2 pm on October 10 and October 17, 2026.

cost.text: Membership and drill fees are not stated on the page.

first_step.how: Become a member through the sign-up link on the website, then come to a drill on October 10 or October 17 at 2 pm.
first_step.basis: The site has a clear join link and lists drills, but does not say whether drills are open to beginners.

records.notes: Legal name is Philadelphia Liberty Tennis Association Inc. The 2023 footer is not evidence. The basis for active is the two listed October 2026 drills; no dated news is posted. The venue street address is not on the page, so no location is recorded. Check the address before listing the venue as a Philadelphia location. The membership sign-up page was not opened.

records.name: Philadelphia Student Press Association
records.summary: A coalition of student-run newsrooms from Philadelphia colleges. It shares resources and mentoring across campuses and helps students move toward professional journalism.
records.what_you_do: Students join as members, volunteer, or host a workshop or panel. The group also plans a free two-day journalism summit for student journalists.

schedule.text: No regular meeting schedule is published. Events are posted as they come up, and the summit date is still to be set.

cost.text: Membership fees are not stated. The summit is described as free.

first_step.how: Use the Join as Member or Volunteer Opportunities links on the Get Involved page.
first_step.basis: The sign-up and volunteer paths are clearly posted. The group serves student journalists, so eligibility is mainly for students.

records.notes: The last-sign-of-life date comes from a homepage photo caption about an event on Feb 19, 2026. The site also lists an Oct 28, 2026 talk run by the World Affairs Council of Philadelphia, which PSPA shows but does not run. A post titled Beyond the Sentence, dated Sep 27 with no year, was not used. The email is the group's own address as published on the site. No phone number is published.

records.name: Philadelphia Virtuosi Chamber Orchestra
records.summary: A chamber orchestra founded in Philadelphia in 1991 that has toured abroad and made recordings. We could not confirm a current season.
records.what_you_do: The orchestra has played concerts, tours and recordings. Whether musicians can still join, or attend a current concert, is not confirmed.

cost.text: Not known. No current season or ticket page was found.

records.notes: Legal name is Philadelphia Virtuosi Chamber Orchestra Inc. The website on the IRS filing, pvco.org, now redirects to a domain-for-sale page, so it is not listed as a contact. The newest dated fact found is a Nov 2014 tour of Russia (Wikipedia). The article does not say whether the orchestra is active. One search found only older pages with no dates after 2014. Status is dormant on that basis. A reviewer should decide whether to keep a dormant group published, or hide it as defunct once closure is confirmed. No current way to join was found. The category is the closest tag for a professional chamber orchestra.

records.name: Philadelphia Youth Action
records.summary: A youth leadership group for middle and high school students in Philadelphia. It trains students in civic leadership, pairs them with mentors and funds student civic projects.
records.what_you_do: Students join one of three programs: Junior Youth Action for 7th and 8th graders, Inspiring Leaders for 9th and 10th graders (a two-year program), and Service Leader for graduates of the first two.

cost.text: Not stated. The page mentions scholarship funds for members and asks for donations, but names no membership fee.

first_step.how: Call 215-867-9464 or email inspire@youthactionteam.org to ask how to join a program, or use the Join the Movement link on the website.
first_step.basis: Each program is described with its grades, and there is a clear way to ask about joining. The page does not describe an application.

records.notes: Legal name Philadelphia Youth Action, Inc. The site says the group has worked with students since 2003. Its newest dated item is a post titled Meeting the Moment: 2026 MLK Day of Service, dated Jan 26, 2026. That is the post date, not necessarily the event date. The post's exact URL was not captured, so the homepage is cited. The page shows no program dates or enrollment steps. A staging domain is mentioned on the page and was not recorded. The IRS P.O. Box matches the site.

records.name: Philly Cheer Elite
records.summary: An all-volunteer cheerleading team in Philadelphia that uses cheer to raise awareness of LGBTQIA+ equality.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer members cheer as a team. Sign up on the group's form to hear about recruitment events.

cost.text: Not stated. The site has a donation link and no membership or tuition fee.

first_step.how: Fill out the general interest form on the join page to be told about recruitment events.
first_step.basis: Open to new volunteers with a clear sign-up. The site does not describe tryout requirements.

records.notes: The only date on the site is a 2019 copyright footer, which is not evidence. probably_active rests on a working site with no dates. No practice or event schedule is published. No tag fits cheerleading exactly; dance_company and lgbtq_social are the closest. The page does not limit membership by identity; community lgbtq reflects the group's stated focus. A mailing address is published on South Street, but it was not recorded because it is not a practice place. The Instagram links were not read.

records.name: Philly Girls Baseball
records.summary: A nonprofit all-girls baseball program for players ages 8 to 18. Players practice at Philadelphia parks and travel to tournaments.
records.what_you_do: Players practice in the spring and summer and play in tournaments. Families register for a practice package or a full travel package.

schedule.text: Outdoor season runs March to October. Sunday afternoon practices run late March to June, with weekday evening practices in summer. The site gives the summer frequency two different ways. Tournament dates for 2026 are listed, including the DMV Series on October 10 and 11.

cost.text: 2026 instructional package is $180 per player, registered on a rolling basis. The 2026 all-inclusive package is $600 per player and its registration closed May 31, 2026. Tournament fees are extra. Scholarships are available by asking the group.

first_step.how: Register for the instructional package through the LeagueApps portal linked from the website, or email info@phillygirlsbaseball.com about a scholarship.
first_step.basis: Registration is clearly posted and there is a no-tournament instructional option, though there is a fee.

records.notes: The newest news item on the site is dated July 11, 2024. The active status rests on the 2026 registration packages and the 2026 tournament listings, including the DMV Series on Oct 10 and 11, 2026. Two 2026 tournaments are labeled Event Completed even though their dates are later, so their status is unclear. The all-inclusive package closed May 31, 2026. This is a girls-only program; no gender tag exists in the community list, so community is empty. No street address or phone number is published, and the practice fields are named but not addressed.

notes: Batch of 15 IRS groups (lead ids irs_990n and irs_bmf). Verdicts: publish 15 (of which 5 are minimal unknown records to be held back: Community Cats, Dramatists Center, Independence Awards, Soccer 2026, Philly Startup Leaders; and Virtuosi is publish with status dormant). Hide 0, not_a_group 0, duplicate 0, out_of_area 0. Searches used 2 of 2 (hard cap reached). Fetches used 19 of 60. Search budget ran out before Dramatists Center, Independence Awards, Soccer 2026 and Philly Startup Leaders could be searched; their websites were unusable (an email address, a name, a dead domain, a host that does not resolve). Two fetches returned blank pages and one directory returned 403, which is listed under blocked. No rate-limit wave was seen; the failures were isolated DNS, connection and empty-page errors. Personal emails and apartment-style IRS street addresses were not recorded. The Crosstown record needs a human look at the candidate flyer on its meeting notice. The Virtuosi record needs a decision on whether a dormant group stays published.
